docs.title: sercol
docs.text: sercol provides Collection, a sequence that filters and groups while keeping its collection type and source metadata, and saves to JSON through serializable. It is the base class for varcode's VariantCollection and EffectCollection and mhctools' BindingPredictionCollection, so their filtering and grouping behave the same.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
python -m pip install sercol

Python 3.11 or later is required; pip installs serializable and pandas 3.

docs.title: Filter and group values
docs.text:
from sercol import Collection

values = Collection([5, 2, 3, 2])
selected = values.filter(lambda value: value >= 3)
groups = values.groupby(lambda value: value % 2)
print(list(selected))
print({key: list(group) for key, group in groups.items()})

[5, 3]
{1: [5, 3], 0: [2, 2]}

filter() returns a collection; groupby() returns a dictionary of collections. Both keep the original collection class and its distinct, sort_key and sources. The original collection is unchanged.

docs.title: Save and reload
docs.text:
Continuing with values above:

restored = Collection.from_json(values.to_json())
print(list(restored))
print(restored == values)

[5, 2, 3, 2]
True

Serialization uses serializable. Elements and constructor state must be supported by that format; callable sorting keys need to be importable when reconstructing the collection.

See select, order and track values for thresholds, multiple grouping keys and source metadata. The API reference lists all collection operations.

docs.title: Collection reference
docs.text:
The full Collection API, after a task index. The guide shows the common methods in use.

Task Method Keep matching elements filter() Group under one or several keys groupby(), multi_groupby() Apply lookup thresholds filter_above_threshold(), filter_any_above_threshold() Preserve metadata while replacing elements clone_with_new_elements() Write record-shaped elements to a table to_dataframe(), to_csv() Save or reload supported objects Inherited to_json(), from_json()

Table conversion expects elements that the serialization helper can turn into field dictionaries. A collection of primitive integers is useful for filtering examples, but is not a record table.

docs.title: Collection
docs.text:
Bases: Serializable

Collection base class with grouping and filtering functions.

docs.title: source property
docs.text:
source

Returns the single source name for a variant collection if it is unique, otherwise raises an error.

docs.title: path property
docs.text:
path

Alternative name for source, maintained for backward compatibility.

docs.title: filenames property
docs.text:
filenames

Base names of the non-empty sources, assuming they are file paths (for example VCF or MAF files).

docs.title: filename property
docs.text:
filename

First entry of filenames (the only one when there is a single source), kept for backward compatibility.

Raises IndexError when the collection has no non-empty source.

docs.title: __init__
docs.text:
__init__(elements, distinct=False, sort_key=None, sources=set([]))

Parameters:

  • elements (list) –

    Collection of any class which is compatible with the sort key

  • distinct (bool, default: False ) –

    Keep only the first occurrence of each element (elements must be hashable) or allow duplicates.

  • sort_key (fn, default: None ) –

    Function which maps each element to a sorting criterion.

  • sources (set, default: set([]) ) –

    Set of files from which this collection was generated.

docs.title: to_dict
docs.text:
to_dict()

Return the constructor arguments needed to rebuild this collection.

This also serves subclasses whose constructor takes the same arguments, such as one that inherits Collection.__init__, so they can be pickled, copied and saved as JSON without their own to_dict.

Returns:

  • dict –

    elements, distinct, sort_key and sources.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If this object's class has a constructor with other arguments. Such a subclass must define its own to_dict.

docs.title: to_dataframe
docs.text:
to_dataframe()

Build a table with one row per element.

Each element is converted with serializable.to_dict, so elements must be dicts, objects with a to_dict method (such as Serializable instances), or objects whose attributes match their constructor arguments.

Returns:

  • DataFrame –

docs.title: to_csv
docs.text:
to_csv(path)

Write to_dataframe() to a CSV file, including its index column.

Parameters:

  • path (str or path - like) –

    Destination file; an existing file is overwritten.

docs.title: clone_with_new_elements
docs.text:
clone_with_new_elements(new_elements, drop_keywords=set([]), rename_dict={}, extra_kwargs={})

Create another Collection of the same class and with same state but possibly different entries. Extra parameters to control which keyword arguments get passed to the initializer are necessary since derived classes have different constructors than the base class.

Parameters:

  • new_elements (list) –

    Elements of the new collection.

  • drop_keywords (set of str, default: set([]) ) –

    Base-class constructor arguments (distinct, sort_key, sources) to leave out.

  • rename_dict (dict, default: {} ) –

    Maps base-class argument names to the names the subclass constructor uses.

  • extra_kwargs (dict, default: {} ) –

    Additional constructor arguments, applied last.

Returns:

  • Collection –

    A new instance of self.__class__.

docs.title: short_string
docs.text:
short_string()

Compact string representation which doesn't print any of the collection elements.

docs.title: to_string
docs.text:
to_string(limit=None)

Create a string representation of this collection, showing up to limit items.

docs.title: filter
docs.text:
filter(filter_fn)

Keep the elements for which filter_fn returns a true value.

Parameters:

  • filter_fn (callable) –

    Takes one element and returns a truthy or falsy value.

Returns:

  • Collection –

    A collection of the same class, built with clone_with_new_elements.

docs.title: groupby
docs.text:
groupby(key_fn)

Group elements by the key key_fn returns for each.

Parameters:

  • key_fn (callable) –

    Takes one element and returns a hashable grouping key.

Returns:

  • dict –

    Maps each key to a collection of the same class, built with clone_with_new_elements from that key's elements in iteration order (so distinct and sort_key still apply).

docs.title: multi_groupby
docs.text:
multi_groupby(key_fn)

Like groupby, but key_fn returns several keys for each element, and the element is added to the group for every one of them.

Parameters:

  • key_fn (callable) –

    Takes one element and returns an iterable of hashable keys.

Returns:

  • dict –

    Maps each key to a collection of the same class.

docs.title: filter_above_threshold
docs.text:
filter_above_threshold(key_fn, value_dict, threshold, default_value=0.0)

Keep elements whose looked-up value is above a threshold.

For example, keep variant effects whose gene expression is above a cutoff.

Parameters:

  • key_fn (callable) –

    Given an element of this collection, returns a key into value_dict

  • value_dict (dict) –

    Dict from keys returned by key_fn to float values

  • threshold (float) –

    Only keep elements whose value in value_dict is above this threshold.

  • default_value (float, default: 0.0 ) –

    Value to use for elements whose key is not in value_dict

Returns:

  • Collection –

    A collection of the same class, as filter returns.

docs.title: filter_any_above_threshold
docs.text:
filter_any_above_threshold(multi_key_fn, value_dict, threshold, default_value=0.0)

Like filter_above_threshold but multi_key_fn returns multiple keys and the element is kept if any of them have a value above the given threshold.

Parameters:

  • multi_key_fn (callable) –

    Given an element of this collection, returns multiple keys into value_dict

  • value_dict (dict) –

    Dict from keys returned by multi_key_fn to float values

  • threshold (float) –

    Only keep elements whose value in value_dict is above this threshold.

  • default_value (float, default: 0.0 ) –

    Value to use for elements whose key is not in value_dict

Returns:

  • Collection –

    A collection of the same class, as filter returns.

docs.title: Documentation style
docs.text:
Follow the PyEnsembl writing guide and the mhctools example.

Put installation and the first useful example on the home page. Give complete imports and concrete inputs, explain the result, and state prerequisites before the reader runs a command. Show output only when it has been checked. Label replaceable paths and templates.

Order guides by common tasks before advanced setup and implementation details. Keep desktop sidebar groups expanded initially and individually collapsible. Split a page when a substantial task or reference needs its own explanation. Preserve useful old links and anchors when moving content.

Use ordinary text for concepts and library names; reserve inline code for literal commands, API names, parameters, paths and values. Keep qualifications, experimental status and scientific limitations beside the claims they qualify.

Use system fonts, a readable line length and restrained headings. Let wide tables and code blocks scroll inside their containers. Avoid repetitive navigation lists in prose and excessive callouts.

Install requirements-docs.txt and run ./docs.sh before opening a PR. Review the home page and a reference page at desktop and narrow widths. Run the repository's required lint and test commands and execute complete examples. Documentation dependencies are separate from runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Select, order and track values
docs.text: This guide covers the Collection options beyond plain filtering and grouping: removing duplicates, sorting, selecting by looked-up values, putting one element in several groups, recording sources, and writing a subclass.

docs.title: Remove duplicates and sort
docs.text:
from sercol import Collection

values = Collection([5, 2, 3, 2], distinct=True, sort_key=abs)
print(list(values))

[2, 3, 5]

distinct=True keeps the first occurrence of each element, in input order, so elements must be hashable. sort_key then sorts what remains; elements with equal keys keep their input order.

docs.title: Select by a value lookup
docs.text:
scores = {"alpha": 2.0, "beta": 0.5}
names = Collection(["alpha", "beta", "unknown"])
selected = names.filter_above_threshold(
    key_fn=lambda name: name,
    value_dict=scores,
    threshold=1.0,
)
print(list(selected))

['alpha']

The comparison is strictly greater than the threshold. Missing keys receive default_value, which defaults to zero. Use filter_any_above_threshold() when each element supplies several lookup keys and any one may qualify.

docs.title: Put an element in several groups
docs.text:
words = Collection(["ab", "bc"])
groups = words.multi_groupby(lambda word: set(word))
print({key: list(groups[key]) for key in sorted(groups)})

{'a': ['ab'], 'b': ['ab', 'bc'], 'c': ['bc']}

multi_groupby() accepts an iterable of keys for each element. Return distinct keys for each element when it should appear only once in each group.

docs.title: Keep source metadata
docs.text:
values = Collection([1, 2, 3], sources={"results.csv"})
selected = values.filter(lambda value: value > 1)
print(selected.source)
print(selected.filenames)

results.csv
['results.csv']

sources labels where values came from; it does not open those files. source requires exactly one source. filenames strips directory components.

docs.title: Extend the collection
docs.text: A subclass should accept the state passed by clone_with_new_elements(): elements, distinct, sort_key and sources, or override that cloning operation. A subclass whose constructor takes exactly those arguments, for example one that inherits Collection.__init__, can be pickled, copied and saved as JSON as it is. A subclass whose constructor takes other arguments must implement its own to_dict() returning them; Collection.to_dict() raises ValueError for it rather than return state its constructor cannot accept.
